newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index rallies at noon led by big firms.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index rallies at noon led by big firms.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index rebounded sharply at midday on Tuesday led by companies that posted strong 1996 results, but analysts said it could come up against technical resistance in the afternoon.
The foreign currency B share index gained 2.76 points or 1.89 percent to 149.11 on tunnover of HK$62.1 million.
"Companies with strong results staged a strong rally as soon as the markets stabilised after yesterday's sharp falls," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

On Monday, the B index closed down 4.47 percent after a leading A share firm, the Shenzhen Development Bank, postponed a shareholders' meeting due to a probe into share trading irregularities, analysts said.
"The index will need some good news to push it pass the 150 resistance point in the afternoon," the Guotai analyst said.
"Investors are still cautious about possible Beijing measures to cool the stock markets," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
The government began to dish out policies to rein in stock speculation at the start of May, after the A and B indices had surged more than 50 percent from the beginning of 1997.

Beijing recently said it would ban state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading and increase the share supply with a 30 billion yuan quota for new domestic share issues to dampen volatility.
The Shenzhen and Shanghai exchanges in the last two weeks suspended trading in a number of A shares for investigations into possible misconduct.
Diesel concern Changchai Co Ltd was the sharpest gainer in the B share market, adding HK$0.53 or 7.96 percent to HK$7.19.
The domestic currency A share index soared 12.27 points or 2.89 percent to 436.51 on turnover of 3.3 billion yuan by noon.
The Shenzhen bank traded at 37.55 yuan, down 0.25 yuan or 0.66 percent, making it the biggest loser in the A share market.
